unit: JPY, METI traditional crafts support budget
note: 「伝統的工芸品産業「支援」補助金 3.6億円」 (successor training, raw materials, new products; 「令和8年度：84件採択（令和7年度採択数：82件）」, subsidy rate 2/3 for associations and makers) and 「「振興」補助金 7.2億円」 (to the Association), 「合計 10.8億円」 (same METI material, pp. 8-10)

unit: JPY an hour, national weighted average minimum wage
note: 「改定額の全国加重平均額は1,177円（昨年度1,121円）」; in force between 1 October and 2 December 2026 by prefecture; highest ¥1,280 (Tokyo), lowest ¥1,085 (Miyazaki) (MHLW, 3 September 2026)

unit: working hours a month used by MHLW to compare the minimum wage with public assistance
note: 「月173.8時間働いた場合」, material 「生活保護と最低賃金」 for the Central Minimum Wages Council's subcommittee on guidelines (second meeting, 10 July 2026), as posted by the Niigata Labour Bureau

unit: JPY scheduled monthly earnings (所定内給与額), all general workers
note: 2025 Basic Survey on Wage Structure, summary (MHLW, March 2026): 「男女計 340,600円（前年比3.1％増）」; June pay, firms with 10 or more employees

unit: JPY scheduled monthly earnings of general workers: ceramic and stone products, wood and paper products, textile and clothing production workers
note: e-Stat, 2025 Basic Survey on Wage Structure, general workers by occupation, table 1 (industries total, firms with 10 or more employees): ¥283.9 thousand, ¥269.7 thousand, ¥221.0 thousand; there is no category for traditional craft workers

unit: EUR a week to 2,000 artists and arts workers
note: 2,000 recipients picked at random from 8,206 eligible applicants (over 9,000 applications), paid from the selection date of 29 August 2022 for three years, extended for six months to February 2026; taxable; 1,000 eligible applicants in a control group paid €650 a year (Department press releases of 28 October 2022 and 19 June 2025)

unit: hours a week more on creative practice than the control group
note: Impact Assessment (2 years), data October 2022 to October 2024: 11 weekly hours more on creative practice; 14 percentage points more likely to have completed new works; 3.5 weekly hours less working in another sector; 15 points less likely to have felt downhearted or depressed and 16 points less likely to have experienced anxiety; life satisfaction 7 against 6

unit: EUR of benefit to society per EUR of public money
note: Alma Economics cost-benefit analysis for the Department: total gross pilot costs about €114 million between 2021 and 2025 (2025 prices); just over €100 million of benefits, mostly wellbeing

unit: EUR from Budget 2026 for the successor scheme
note: '2,000 eligible artists will be selected to receive the payment of €325 per week. The payment will be for 3 years'; 3-year cycles; selection by anonymised random sampling (Department, 10 February 2026; guidelines of 1 April 2026)

unit: applications to the successor scheme
note: EY selection report of 31 July 2026 (published 4 November 2026); applications open 15 April to 12 May 2026; payments backdated to September 2026; €34.4 million in Budget 2027 (Department, 13 October 2026)

unit: applicants notified on 15 October and on 12 November 2026
note: 'The Department commenced communication to 780 applicants ... on Thursday 15 October and a further 450 applicants will be notified today'; a further tranche before Christmas
